newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says US Fed hike not to impact Thai rates.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says US Fed hike not to impact Thai rates.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday a rise in U.S. interest rates was unlikely to impact Thai rates and the government remained keen to see a reduction in local rates.

"The Federal Reserve's hike in U.S. interest rates is unlikely to have much impact on our interest rates because the rise was very small," Amnuay told reporters. "It will also not change our policy which wants domestic interest rates to be lower."
The U.S. Federal Reserve on Tuesday raised its federal funds lending rate target by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
Amnuay said he did not disagree with market expectations that Thai interest rates should decline about one percentage point from current levels.
Thailand's prime lending rate stood at 13.25 percent, one of the highest in the region.
The minister said the Bank of Thailand could induce lower interest rates by injecting short-term funds through its bond repurchase window.
But he said the central bank would also seek to prevent excessive liquidity which may emerge after the launch of about 78 billion baht government pension funds this week.
"We don't want to see the brimming water overflow...the central bank has auctioned out additional 20 billion baht bonds last week and will float another 30 billion baht this Friday."
